motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of improving the efficiency and performance of masked language models (MLMs) for natural language processing tasks, particularly in generating coherent and coherent-sounding text. While diffusion models have shown success in various domains, such as image generation, video generation, and audio modeling, their application to natural language remains a complex task due to the discrete nature of language. Existing approaches like Masked Language Diffusion (MLD) and Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLM) have been proposed to address this challenge, but they come with significant limitations. MLD, inspired by image-based masked diffusion, introduces a mask matrix that varies with each forward pass, making it difficult for the model to learn coherent text. MDLM, which removes the mask and treats each token as a binary random variable, can lose coherent information during the denoising process. Additionally, the forward pass in autoregressive models like GPT requires an exponential number of parameters, and standard autoregressive models can suffer from degenerate behavior where the model only learns the 'noise' distribution. These limitations highlight the need for a new approach that can efficiently and effectively learn both coherent and incoherent language without losing information. The paper introduces Coherent Masked Diffusion (CoMD), a novel framework that addresses these challenges by using a fixed mask matrix and a coherent loss term, aiming to improve both inference and training efficiency while maintaining or enhancing model performance.
idea: The paper presents Coherent Masked Diffusion (CoMD), a novel framework that extends Masked Language Diffusion (MLD) to more efficiently and effectively learn coherent and incoherent language. CoMD introduces three key innovations: 1) a fixed mask matrix that is independent of the masked-out token, 2) a coherent loss term that optimizes the probability of coherent generations without requiring additional samples per training step, and 3) a variable time parameter to guide the coherent probability towards the ground truth coherent probability. These innovations aim to address the limitations of existing MLD implementations and autoregressive models, leading to improved inference and training efficiency and better performance on coherent tasks.
title: CoMD: Coherent Masked Diffusion
abstract: Masked language models (MLMs) have shown promise in natural language processing, but struggle with generating coherent and coherent-sounding text. In this work, we present Coherent Masked Diffusion (CoMD), a novel framework that extends Masked Language Diffusion to more efficiently and more effectively learn coherent and incoherent language. CoMD is built on Masked Language Diffusion (MLD), a recently proposed framework that models text generation as an inverse denoising diffusion process. Unlike MLD, CoMD uses a fixed mask matrix that is independent of the masked-out token and optimizes the probability of coherent generations with a novel coherent loss term without requiring additional samples per training step. Additionally, CoMD uses a variable time parameter to guide the coherent probability towards the ground truth coherent probability. Both inference and training computation are constant with respect to the length of the text. Empirically, CoMD outperforms previous methods on multiple coherent benchmarks. Furthermore, CoMD achieves an inference speedup of 7.3x and 10.5x over MLD and MDLM, respectively, and is significantly more compute and parameter efficient than autoregressive models.

Experimental_Setup.name: Performance Comparison
Experimental_Setup.description: This experiment compares the performance of CoMD with other next-token prediction frameworks on image and text data, including logic puzzles. The models evaluated include MLD and MDLM. For image data, CoMD uses an 8-layer convolutional model trained on ImageNet, and for text, CoMD uses a 4-layer transformer trained on the SlimPajama dataset with 512 embedding dimensions. The evaluation metrics include OOD perplexity, coherent/incoherent accuracy, and puzzle-solving rate. The datasets used are MNIST, kaggle-mnist, Sudoku, and logic puzzles by Kitouni et al. (2025). The hyperparameters include a max length of 128, a learning rate of 8e-5, a batch size of 128, and the AdamW optimizer with linear decay. Inference speedups are measured with 1 RTX A5000 GPU.

Experimental_Setup.name: SlimPajama Test
Experimental_Setup.description: This experiment evaluates CoMD's performance on a spectrum of text lengths with a test benchmark generated from the SlimPajama dataset. The benchmark requires models to generate coherent/sounding text with optional prefixes. The test suite generates 5000 samples of each length from 1 to 1024, with prefixes ranging from 0 to 384 tokens. The evaluation metrics include coherent/clean perplexity and coherent/incoherent accuracy. The coherent/clean perplexity is evaluated on both original and reversed text to assess the long-range time travel language model.

Experimental_Setup.name: Ablations
Experimental_Setup.description: This experiment ablates the three proposed innovations in CoMD: fixed mask, coherent loss, and time shift. The experiment aims to understand the contributions of each innovation by removing each term from the CoMD loss function and evaluating the performance on coherent/incoherent tasks. The models evaluated include CoMD, CoMD without fixed mask, CoMD without coherent loss, CoMD without time shift, and CoMD without either coherent loss or time shift. The evaluation metrics include coherent/incoherent accuracy and perplexity on Sudoku and SlimPajama test.
